STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.claim: After recalling worldly blessings, the surah tells of Noah's struggle against his people's denial and rebuke and his journey in the ark.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.anchor: the sūrah narrates the story of Noah, his struggles with the denial and rebuke of his people, and his journey in the ark (vv. 23–41)

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r9.claim: The pronoun هي is understood from context: the people had denied resurrection, so their mocking question implies that only their worldly life exists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r9.anchor: وقالوا إن هي هذا الضمير يفسره سياق الكلام لأنهم قبل أنكروا المعاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains هي as standing for الحياة, identified by the following predicate; إن then negates the genus, yielding that there is no life except worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p561/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هذا ضمير لا يعلم ما يعنى به إلا بما يتلوه من بيانه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r1.claim: نموت ونحيا means some die and others are born: one generation passes and another arrives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r1.anchor: نموت ونحيا أي يموت بعض ويولد بعض ينقرض قرن ويأتي قرن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r2.claim: The deniers restrict life to worldly generations and reject resurrection for judgment, expressing the unbelief of the materialist deniers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r2.anchor: ثم أكدوا ما حصروه من أن لا حياة إلا حياتهم وحرموا بانتفاء بعثهم من قبورهم للجزاء وهذا هو كفر الدهرية

TABATABAI:23:23-54/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r5.claim: “We die and live” means that some people die and others are born in this world, continuing the cycle; the author mentions transmigration of souls as another possible sense, common among pagans, but says it fits the context poorly.
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r5.anchor: أي يموت قوم منا في الدنيا ويحيا آخرون فيها لا نزال كذلك

TABATABAI:23:23-54/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r6.claim: The phrase “we die and live” could instead refer to transmigration, as souls leave one body at death and enter another human or nonhuman body; this was common among idolaters and sometimes called birth after birth.
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r6.anchor: فإن التناسخ مذهب شائع عند الوثنيين وربما عبروا عنه بالولادة بعد الولادة

SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r1.claim: The pronoun hī is explained by context: the intended sense is that their life is only this worldly life.

SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the pronoun's referent is only known from what follows; the original was al-ḥayātu, replaced by hī because the predicate identifies it.
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " هذا ضمير لا يعلم ما يراد به

SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r3.claim: Al-Samīn says classifying this as a phrase explained by what follows in both wording and syntax does not apply to al-Zamakhsharī's quoted explanation, despite an attribution to him.
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r3.anchor: إلى الزمخشري متعلقا بهذا الكلام الذي نقلته

SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r4.claim: The clause explains the claim that their life consists only of this cycle.
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r4.anchor: جملة مفسرة لما ادعوه من أن حياتهم

SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r5.claim: Al-Samīn rejects using the verb order to prove that wāw does not imply sequence: apparently some die and others live successively, each generation replacing another.
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r5.anchor: الظاهر من معناها: يموت البعض منا، ويحيا آخرون

SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r6.claim: One interpretation is that the speakers mean that they themselves die while their children live on.

SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r7.claim: Another interpretation is that they believe in return to life: they die, then live again after that death.
SAMIN-DURR:23:37/r7.anchor: وقيل: القوم يعتقدون الرجعة أي: نموت ثم نحيا

ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r3.claim: The deniers assert that earthly life is all there is, deny resurrection, and accuse the messenger of inventing lies about God.
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r3.anchor: There is no life beyond our life in this world: we die and we live [but once], and we shall never be raised

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.claim: He calls the passage's close with resurrection natural: resurrection is the final link in the sequence of life and its development.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.anchor: فأنتَ ترى أن ختام الآيات هذه بالبعث، هو الختمُ الطبيعي، وهو الحلقة النهائية في سلسلة الحياة وتطورها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r1.claim: The underlying wording is إن الحياة إلا حياتنا الدنيا; the pronoun replaces الحياة because the predicate identifies it, a permitted backward reference when the predicate explains its antecedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r1.anchor: أصله إن الحياة إلا حياتنا الدنيا ثم وضع الضمير موضع الحياة لأن الخبر يدل عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r2.claim: An objection notes that the predicate is qualified, so including that qualification in the pronoun's antecedent would make the sentence tautological; the response is that a pronoun may refer to the noun without its qualification.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r2.anchor: واعترض بأن الخبر موصوف فتلاحظ الصفة في ضميره

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r3.claim: Al-Alusi's preferred explanation is that the pronoun refers to the mentally understood genus of life, yielding their intended denial: no life exists except worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r3.anchor: بأن الضمير عائد على ما يفهم من جنس الحياة ليفيد الحمل ما قصدوه من نفي البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r4.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r4.claim: Al-Kashf says the pronoun refers to a mentally familiar concept signaled by what follows, as in هذا أخوك, rather than repeating the predicate as its antecedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r4.anchor: وفي الكشف ليس المعنى النفس النفس لأنه لا يصلح الثاني حينئذ تفسيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r5.claim: The discussion illustrates backward reference with the expression هي العرب تقول ما شاءت and the line هي النفس ما حملتها تتحمل وللدهر أيام تجوز وتعدل.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r6.claim: This clause explains their claim that life is only worldly: some die and others are born in turn, not that individuals live again after death, which would contradict their denial of resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r6.anchor: جملة مفسرة لما ادعوه من أن الحياة هي الحياة الدنيا وأرادوا بذلك يموت بعضنا ويولد بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r7.claim: Other proposed senses are death as nonexistence before birth, or the children's survival counting as their parents' continued life; al-Alusi considers these explanations far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r7.anchor: أرادوا بالموت العدم السابق على الوجود أو أرادوا بالحياة بقاء أولادهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r8.claim: A further proposal is that they believed in transmigration: a departed soul successively enters newly formed bodies; al-Alusi says he does not regard this proposal as far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r8.anchor: أن القوم كانوا قائلين بالتناسخ فحياتهم بتعلق النفس التي فارقت أبدانهم بأبدان أخر عنصرية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r9.claim: The proposed sequence may resemble one reading of Jesus' words in 3:55: conjunction with wāw does not require chronological order, so their intended life could precede death.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى لعيسى عليه السلام ( إني متوفيك ورافعك إلى ) على قول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r10.claim: They may actually have said نحيا ونموت, with the order changed in the report to fit إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r10.anchor: ويحتمل أنهم قالوا نحيا ونموت إلا أنه لما حكى عنهم قيل ( نموت ونحيا ) ليكون

ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r11.claim: Their final clause makes the denial of resurrection continuous and emphatic.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p32#2/r11.anchor: ثم المراد بقولهم ( وما نحن ) الخ استمرار النفي وتأكيده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r9.claim: The pronoun hiya refers to the present worldly life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r9.anchor: {إن هي} يعنون الدنيا، {إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r10.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r10.claim: One explanation reverses the order to “we live and die,” since they deny resurrection after death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r10.anchor: قيل فيه تقديم وتأخير، أي: نحيا ونموت لأنهم كانوا ينكرون البعث بعد الموت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r11.claim: Another explanation is that fathers die while their children live.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r12.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r12.claim: A further explanation is that some people die while others live.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r13.claim: They deny being raised and spread abroad after death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r13.anchor: وما نحن بمبعوثين} بمنشرين بعد الموت

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r1.claim: The underlying phrasing was inna al-ḥayāta illā ḥayātunā al-dunyā; the pronoun replaces the first life to avoid repetition and signal its identity is self-evident.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r1.anchor: أصله إن الحياة { إلا حياتنا الدنيا } فأقيم الضمير مقام الأولى

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r2.claim: They claim no life exists beyond this world; the negative in applies to hiyā, which signifies life as a genus and has the force of lā negating a genus.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r2.anchor: ومعناه لا حياة إلا هذه الحياة لأن { إن } نافية دخلت على { هي } التي في معنى الحياة

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r3.claim: Some people die while others are born.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r3.anchor: يموت بعضنا ويولد بعض. { وما نحن بمبعوثين }

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r4.claim: The line هي النفس ما حملتها تتحمل is cited as poetic evidence for replacing the first noun with a pronoun to avoid repetition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:37/r4.anchor: كقوله: هي النفس ما حملتها تتحمل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r1.claim: Their emphatic denial that resurrection is possible leads directly to the claim that worldly life is the only life they can have.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r1.anchor: في التبعيد كأنهم قالوا : إنا لا نبعث أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r2.claim: They explain worldly life as some people dying while new people are born after them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r2.anchor: أي يموت منا من هو موجود

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200/r3.claim: They deny being raised after death.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r1.claim: This sentence can explain and argue for their dismissal of the promised resurrection; it is separated from the previous sentence because it supplies the reason.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r2.claim: The pronoun deliberately precedes its referent حياتنا, first leaving the topic vague and then clarifying it; the later noun functions as an explanatory apposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r2.anchor: وهذا من مواضع عود الضمير على ما بعده إذا كان ما بعده بيانا له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r3.claim: هي is not the pronoun of the story: it is explained by a singular noun, not a clause, and the construction with لا النافية للجنس also rules out that reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r3.anchor: ولأنه في الآية مفسر بالمفرد لا بالجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r4.claim: الدنيا means the nearer, present life; the negation means there is no life after this one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r4.anchor: والدنيا : مؤنث الأدنى ، أي القريبة بمعنى الحاضرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r5.claim: Their ‘we die and live’ can mean successive generations die and are born, or that some die and do not return while the living continue until they die.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r5.anchor: ومعنى { نحيا } : نولد ، أي يموت من يموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r6.claim: The waw in this phrase does not imply chronological order between dying and living.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p55/r6.anchor: والواو لا تفيد ترتيبا بين معطوفها والمعطوف عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p56/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p56/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p56/r1.claim: The denial of resurrection is coordinated with the preceding claim, whose restriction implies only immediate life and death; the nominal form strengthens the assertion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p56/r1.anchor: وأفاد صوغ الخبر في الجملة الاسمية تقوية مدلوله وتحقيقه

BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r5.claim: Here in is a negating particle meaning mā, so the phrase means this life is only our worldly life.
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r5.anchor: إن بمعنى ما ، أي ما الحياة

BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r6.claim: They describe worldly life as near and perishing.
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r6.anchor: أي ما الحياة {الا حياتنا الدنيا} الدانية الفانية

BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r7.claim: The phrase either means some die while others are born until the age ends, or that people experience worldly life and then death with no life afterward.
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r7.anchor: أي يموت بعضنا ويولد بعض إلى انقراض العصر

BURSEVI:v6p59/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59/r1.claim: They deny being raised after death, as Hud says they claim; their hearts are blind to the fact that restoration is easier than initial creation and that the creator of existence and nonexistence can restore it.
BURSEVI:v6p59/r1.anchor: بمنشرين بعد الموت كما تزعم يا هود انظر كيف عميت قلوبهم حتى لم يروا أن الإعادة أهون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r20.claim: They deny any existence beyond this life: one generation dies and disappears, while another arises.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r20.anchor: أرادوا أنه لا وجود لنا غير هذا الوجود، وإنما تموت منا طائفة فتذهب وتجيء طائفة جديدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r21.claim: This denial of resurrection is the unbelief of the materialist eternalists (Dahriyya).

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r1.claim: The deniers mean that the only life is the present worldly one and that no life follows death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r1.anchor: يعنون ما الحياة إلا ما نحن فيه و ليس بعد الموت حياة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r2.claim: One answer is that they mean some people die while their children live, so generations alternate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r2.anchor:
فعنه ثلاثة أجوبة ذكرها الزجاج
أحدها نموت ويحيا أولادنا فكأنهم قالوا يموت قوم ويحيا قوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r3.claim: A second answer is that they said we live and die; the conjunction wāw coordinates without imposing sequence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r3.anchor: والثاني نحيا ونموت لأن الواو للجمع لا للترتيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r4.claim: A third answer is that humans begin as lifeless matter, then live, and then die.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p472/r4.anchor:
ذكرها الزجاج
أحدها نموت ويحيا أولادنا فكأنهم قالوا يموت قوم ويحيا قوم
والثاني نحيا ونموت لأن الواو للجمع لا للترتيب
والثالث أبتداؤنا موات

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r2.claim: One denial means that people live for a time, then die, with no resurrection afterward.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r2.anchor: قيل: نحيا حينا ثم نموت ولا إعادة بعد ذلك

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r3.claim: Another explanation is that some people die while others remain alive.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r3.anchor: وقيل: يموت قوم منا ويحيا قوم

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r4.claim: A further explanation is that the fathers die and their children live on.

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r18.claim: The chiefs contradict themselves: they call following the messenger a loss but not idol worship, although idols cannot help or harm; they reject a living messenger while worshipping an inanimate body.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r18.anchor: وتدل على مناقضة القوم؛ لأنهم جعلوا اتباع الرسول خسرانا، ولم يجعلوا عبادة الصنم خسرانا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.claim: The pronoun hiyā is understood through the following explanation; the clause stands in place of “there is no life but our worldly life.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r6.anchor: هذا ضمير لا يعلم ما يعني به إلا بما يتلوه من بيانه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.claim: The negative inna governs hiyā, which denotes life as a genus, giving the force of lā negating the whole genus.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r7.anchor: لأن ( إن ) النافية دخلت على ( هي ) التي في معنى الحياة الدالة على الجنس فنفتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r8.claim: They mean some people die while others are born: one generation passes away and another comes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r8.anchor: أي يموت بعض ويولد بعض ، ينقرض قرن ويأتي قرن آخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r9.claim: They accuse the messenger of inventing claims about his commissioning and resurrection after death, and say they will not believe him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r9.anchor: ثم قالوا : ما هو إلا مفتر على الله فيما يدعيه من استنبائه له

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r1.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r1.claim: Ibn ʿIsa reads the phrase as meaning that some of their people die while others live.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r1.anchor: أحدها : يموت منا قوم ويحيا منا قوم , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r2.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Salam reads it as one generation dying and another being born; al-Kalbi specifies fathers die while children live.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r2.anchor: الثاني : يموت قوم ويولد قوم , قاله يحيى بن سلام , قال الكلبي , يموت الآباء ويحيا الأبناء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara says the order is reversed: “we live and die,” with no resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه مقدم ومؤخر معناه نحيا ونموت وما نحن بمبعوثين , قاله ابن شجرة .

MUQATIL:23:35-37/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r3.claim: Their claim is that one generation dies and others born from their descendants live, in an endless cycle.
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r3.anchor: { إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا } يعنى نموت نحن ويحيا آخرون من أصلابنا

MUQATIL:23:35-37/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r4.claim: They deny being resurrected after death; Muqatil notes a parallel in Surat al-Jathiya.
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r4.anchor: { وما نحن بمبعوثين } [آية: 37] بعد الموت مثلها فى الجاثية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r1.claim: The pronoun “it” has no clear referent until the following phrase explains it; it originally stood for “life.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r1.anchor: هذا ضمير لا يعلم ما يعنى به غلا بما يتلوه من بيانه وأصله ان الحياة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r2.claim: The deniers claim there is no life except the worldly life they experience.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r2.anchor: والمعنى لا حياة إلا هذه الحياة التى نحن فيها ودنت منا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r3.claim: The negative particle in enters upon a pronoun denoting the genus of life, so the construction has the force of lā negating the genus.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r3.anchor: لأن ان النافية دخلت على هى التى فى معنى الحياة الدالة على الجنس فنفتها فوازنت لا التى لنفى الجنس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r4.claim: The phrase can mean that some die and others are born, one generation replaced by another.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r4.anchor: أى يموت بعض ويولد بعض ينقوض قرن فيأتى قرن آخر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r5.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r5.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masud read the phrase in reversed order, “we live and die.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r5.anchor: أو فيه تقديم وتأخير أى نحيا ونموت وهو قراءة ابى وابن مسعود رضى الله عنهما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#4/r6.claim: They deny being raised after death.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r1.claim: The pronoun hi refers to this worldly life: they claim there is no life beyond the present one, denying an afterlife after resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r1.anchor: «هي» كناية عن الدنيا أي ما الحياة إلا ما نحن فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r2.claim: One answer to how they say “we die and live” while denying resurrection is that people begin as lifeless drops of semen and then live in this world.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r2.anchor: نكون مواتا، أي نطفا ثم نحيا في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r3.claim: Another answer takes the order as reversed: “we live and die,” as in the paired commands in Ali Imran.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r3.anchor: وقيل: فيه تقديم وتأخير أي إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r4.claim: A further explanation is that the ancestors die and their descendants live.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:37/r5.claim: They deny being raised after death.

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r11.claim: By saying we die and live, they mean that some people die while others live, denying any individual return or resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r11.anchor: بل أرادوا أن البعض يموت والبعض يحيا

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r12.claim: They conclude that there is no resurrection and then infer that the prophet fabricated a lie against God and that they will not believe him.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r12.anchor: ولما فرغوا من الطعن في صحة الحشر بنوا عليه الطعن في نبوته

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r4.claim: The pronoun in in hiya has no clear antecedent until the following words explain it; the underlying wording is in al-ḥayātu illā ḥayātunā al-dunyā.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r4.anchor: ضمير لا يعلم ما يعني به إلا بما يتلوه

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r5.claim: The pronoun replaces al-ḥayāh because the predicate makes its referent clear.

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r6.claim: The meaning is that no life exists except the present worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r6.anchor: والمعنى لا حياة إلا هذه الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r7.claim: The negative in is used with hiya in a genus-denying sense, equivalent to lā negating the genus.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r7.anchor: إن النافية دخلت على هي التي في معنى الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r8.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r8.claim: The poet's line, “the soul: whatever burden you give it, it bears,” illustrates use of a pronoun whose sense is supplied by the predicate.

STUDYQURAN:23:37/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r1.claim: This denial resembles 6:29, while adding that people die and live.
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r1.anchor: This verse is similar to 6:29, but it adds we die and we live

STUDYQURAN:23:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r2.claim: The added phrase means that there is only the life and death of this world.
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r2.anchor: meaning that there is only the life and death of this world (R)

STUDYQURAN:23:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r3.claim: Alternatively, some die and others take their place.
STUDYQURAN:23:37/r3.anchor: and that some die and others take their place (Ṭ)

TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r1.claim: The deniers say there is no life beyond the present worldly life: some people die while others are born, and no one is resurrected after death.
TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما نحن بمبعوثين قال: " يقول: ليس آخرة ولا بعث

TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says they deny an afterlife and resurrection: one generation dies and another comes, like crops being harvested and sprouting; he cites other deniers of resurrection and the Hour.
TAB-FULL:v17p44#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا نموت ونحيا وما نحن بمبعوثين قال: " يقول: ليس آخرة ولا بعث

TABRISI:23:35-40/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r16.claim: The deniers claim only the present, familiar worldly life exists.
TABRISI:23:35-40/r16.anchor: إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا } أي ليس الحياة إلا الحياة التي نحن فيها القريبة منا

TABRISI:23:35-40/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r17.claim: They mean some die while others live, with no resurrection.
TABRISI:23:35-40/r17.anchor: أي يموت قوم منا ويحيا قوم ولا نبعث

TABRISI:23:35-40/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r18.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:23:35-40/r18.claim: Al-Kalbi says fathers die and children live after them.
TABRISI:23:35-40/r18.anchor: وقيل: يموت الآباء ويحيا الأبناء عن الكلبي

TABRISI:23:35-40/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r19.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:23:35-40/r19.claim: Another explanation says some people die and others are born.

TABRISI:23:35-40/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r20.claim: The deniers reject being raised after death.
TABRISI:23:35-40/r20.anchor: وما نحن بمبعوثين } بعد ذلك { إن هو إلا رجل

THALABI:v7p46#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46#2/r7.claim: In the denial ‘it is only our worldly life,’ the pronoun refers to life in this world.
THALABI:v7p46#2/r7.anchor: إن هي يعنون الدنيا إلا حياتنا الدنيا

THALABI:v7p46#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46#2/r8.claim: ‘We die and live’ means that fathers die and their children live.
THALABI:v7p46#2/r8.anchor: نموت ونحيا يموت الآباء ويحيى الأبناء

THALABI:v7p46#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46#2/r9.claim: The speakers reject being raised after death.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r1.claim: هي refers to life; the speakers deny any life beyond the present worldly one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r1.anchor: كناية عن الحياة، ودل عليها قوله: {إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r2.claim: People die and their children remain, then those children die and their descendants remain; al-Kalbi and Muqatil agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: أي نهلك نحن ويبقى أبناؤنا، ويهلك أبناؤنا ويبقى أبناؤهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r3.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r3.claim: Others say some of the people die while others live.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p583/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: أي يموت قوم منا ويحيا آخرون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r3.claim: They mean only the near, present life in this world.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r3.anchor: يعني: الحياة الدانية في هذه الدار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r4.claim: They describe generations replacing one another: the fathers die and the children live.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r4.anchor: نموت ونحيا } يموت الآباء، ويحيا الأولاد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r5.claim: Their claim that they die and live means that they die and are born.

ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.claim: The people dismiss bodily resurrection from dust and bones as impossibly remote, claim worldly life is all there is, and say one generation dies as another is born, so they should enjoy this low life.
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.anchor: kimimiz bir taraftan ölür, kimimiz de yeni doğar hayata geliriz, böyle gider

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.claim: Opponents of prophets were often wealthy elites content with the order because it served their interests; they feared afterlife accountability and a society conscious of universal rights and justice would threaten their status.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.anchor: bunlar umumiyetle hak peygamberin getirdiği sistemi kendi toplumsal ve ekonomik statüleri için tehlikeli görmüşler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.claim: Since the Qur’an answers these denials of the prophet’s person and of the afterlife elsewhere, this passage only warns of the rejecters’ painful fate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.anchor: burada bir defa daha tekrarlanmasına gerek görülmemiş, sadece uğrayacakları acı âkıbete dikkat çekilmekle yetinilmiştir

BURHAN:v1p116/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p116/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p116/r10.claim: Al-Muʾminūn adds نموت to the denial of resurrection found in al-Anʿām.
